chains.title: Alt T strengthens CEBPA binding at a SORT1 enhancer
chains.element: The variant lies in an active distal enhancer-like cCRE (dELS) that is occupied by CEBPA in HepG2.
chains.cell_type: Liver/hepatocyte-line context; HepG2 ChIP is a proxy for Hep 3B2.1-7, where CEBPA is highly expressed.

links.claim: CEBPA is the best-supported C/EBP-family candidate at this element: it is occupied at the variant-containing element in HepG2 (E04), is highly expressed in the exact DepMap context Hep 3B2.1-7 (E20), and C/EBP allele-specific SORT1 enhancer literature is indexed by the E19 search. Alt T is proposed to strengthen CEBPA binding based on C/EBP-site literature/motif logic. No QBiC-SELEX model for CEBPA is supplied, so this allele-specific direction is not directly measured by the provided evidence.

The variant sits in cCRE EH38E1374646, a dELS with DNase/H3K27ac/H3K4me3 signal, and CEBPA is among the bound factors at this active element. E03 z-scores are maxima over ENCODE biosamples, not HepG2-specific.

Alt T is associated with higher SORT1 expression in liver (NES +1.27, p 3.1e-54), and SORT1 has the strongest L2G support at this locus (0.99). This supports SORT1 as a target gene with the stated direction, though not CEBPA mediation.

CEBPA is expressed at 141.33 TPM in Hep 3B2.1-7 (rank 18/1626 TFs; 99.2th percentile), and the ENCODE ChIP evidence is from the liver-cancer-line proxy HepG2; liver SORT1 eQTLs support the liver context.

Most strongest GWAS lipid rows report G as the high-cholesterol risk allele, while alt T increases SORT1 in liver; if increased SORT1 lowers LDL cholesterol, T would be protective. One LDL row reports effect allele T, so the GWAS direction is not fully uniform. E18 provides literature titles, not quoted functional experiments.

predictions: Allele-specific CEBPA ChIP-qPCR or EMSA will show stronger CEBPA binding on alt T than ref G.
A SORT1 enhancer reporter in liver cells will be more active with alt T than ref G.
CEBPA knockdown/knockout will attenuate the alt-T effect on SORT1 expression.
falsified_if: Allele-specific CEBPA binding at rs12740374 is not stronger on alt T than ref G in hepatocyte/liver-cell assays.
CEBPA loss-of-function does not attenuate the alt-T effect on SORT1 expression.
The variant effect on SORT1 is fully explained by a linked variant or by another TF.

chains.title: No TF-mediated effect; linked causal variant, CELSR2 UTR effect, or passenger explanation
predictions: No allele-specific TF binding or enhancer activity will be found at chr1:109274968 after controlling for linked variants.
The causal variant will lie elsewhere in the same credible set, in another nearby cCRE, or the signal will reflect a CELSR2 UTR/transcript effect rather than a TF-mediated enhancer effect.
falsified_if: A validated allele-specific TF binding or enhancer-activity difference at this exact base is demonstrated.
The SORT1/LDL association is shown to be caused by rs12740374 itself rather than a linked variant.

chains.title: Alt T strengthens CEBPA binding and raises CELSR2
chains.element: The variant lies in an active dELS and is also annotated as a CELSR2 3_prime_UTR_variant, so the same enhancer/UTR region could influence CELSR2.
chains.cell_type: Liver/hepatocyte-line context; HepG2 ChIP is a proxy for Hep 3B2.1-7, where CEBPA is highly expressed.

links.claim: CEBPA is occupied at the variant-containing element in HepG2, is highly expressed in Hep 3B2.1-7, and C/EBP allele-specific SORT1-enhancer literature is indexed by the E19 search. Alt T is proposed to strengthen CEBPA binding. No QBiC-SELEX model for CEBPA is supplied, so the direction is inferred rather than directly measured here.
The variant lies in an active dELS (E03) and is also annotated as a CELSR2 3_prime_UTR_variant (E01), so CELSR2 is a plausible target of the same regulatory region.

Alt T is associated with higher CELSR2 expression in liver (NES +1.04, p 9.4e-34), and CELSR2 has high L2G support (0.96-0.98). This supports CELSR2 as a target gene with the stated direction, though not CEBPA mediation.
CEBPA is highly expressed in Hep 3B2.1-7, HepG2 ChIP provides liver-cell occupancy, and CELSR2 eQTLs are observed in liver.

Alt T increases CELSR2 in liver, and CELSR2 is genetically associated with lipid traits. The phenotype direction is inferential because E18 supplies titles, not quoted functional experiments, and the GWAS lipid direction in E15 is not fully uniform.

predictions: Allele-specific CEBPA ChIP or EMSA will show stronger binding on alt T than ref G.
A CELSR2 3'UTR/enhancer reporter will show an alt-T effect in liver cells.
CEBPA loss-of-function will attenuate the alt-T effect on CELSR2 expression.
falsified_if: Allele-specific CEBPA binding at rs12740374 is not stronger on alt T than ref G.
CEBPA loss-of-function does not attenuate the alt-T effect on CELSR2 expression.
CELSR2 expression is unaffected by the variant after controlling for linked variants.

chains.title: Ref G-bound FOXA1 represses SORT1
chains.element: The variant lies in an active dELS occupied by FOXA1.
chains.cell_type: Liver/hepatocyte-line context; FOXA1 is expressed in Hep 3B2.1-7 and bound in HepG2.

links.claim: FOXA1 occupies the variant-containing element in HepG2 and is highly expressed in the exact DepMap context Hep 3B2.1-7 (53.15 TPM; rank 84/1626). Ref G is proposed to bind FOXA1 more strongly, but no QBiC-SELEX model for FOXA1 is supplied and no allele-specific FOXA1 ChIP/EMSA is provided.
The variant lies in an active dELS (E03), and FOXA1 ChIP-seq peaks contain the variant in HepG2 (E05).

If ref G-bound FOXA1 represses SORT1, loss of FOXA1 binding on alt T would derepress SORT1, matching the alt-T-associated increase in liver SORT1 expression. No perturbation evidence shows FOXA1 represses SORT1.
FOXA1 is expressed in Hep 3B2.1-7 and bound in HepG2; SORT1 eQTLs are seen in liver.

Higher SORT1 from alt T is proposed to lower LDL cholesterol and MI risk, opposite to the high-cholesterol risk association of G. The phenotype direction remains inferential because E18 gives titles, not quoted functional experiments, and E15 has one LDL row with effect allele T.

predictions: Allele-specific FOXA1 ChIP or EMSA will show stronger binding on ref G than alt T.
FOXA1 depletion will increase SORT1 expression if FOXA1 is a repressor at this element.
FOXA1 loss-of-function will attenuate the variant effect on SORT1 if FOXA1 mediates it.
falsified_if: FOXA1 binding at the variant is not stronger on ref G than alt T.
FOXA1 knockdown reduces rather than increases SORT1 expression.
No FOXA1-dependent effect on SORT1 is observed.

grades_v0.reason: E04 provides occupancy evidence: CEBPA is listed among bound, expressed TFs with a binding model in HepG2. However, there is no allele-specific ChIP, reporter, or QBiC-SELEX evidence showing alt T binds CEBPA more strongly; the direction is only proposed. CEBPA is also one of many bound TFs, with no rationale for choosing CEBPA over other C/EBP-family factors.

E03 directly places the variant in cCRE EH38E1374646, a dELS, with DNase/H3K27ac/H3K4me3 signal; E04 confirms CEBPA occupancy at this active element in HepG2. Caveat: E03 z-scores are maxima over biosamples, not HepG2-specific.

E17 shows alt T is associated with higher SORT1 expression in liver (NES +1.27, p 3.1e-54), and E16 gives SORT1 the strongest L2G score (0.99). This supports SORT1 as a target gene with the stated direction, though not CEBPA mediation.
E04 and E17 support a liver/HepG2 context, but HepG2 is an explicit proxy for Hep 3B2.1-7 and the evidence does not directly show CEBPA expression or allele-specific CEBPA occupancy in Hep 3B2.1-7.

E15 supports G as the high-cholesterol risk allele in the strongest rows, and E17 supports alt T increasing SORT1, which is directionally consistent with T being protective if SORT1 lowers LDL. But no cited evidence directly shows SORT1 manipulation lowers LDL or MI; E18 provides only titles, not abstract quotes, and one E15 LDL row reports effect allele T, which conflicts with the main direction.

E05 supports FOXA1 occupancy at the variant in HepG2 and high FOXA1 expression in Hep 3B2.1-7, but there is no allele-specific ChIP or QBiC-SELEX evidence showing ref G binds FOXA1 more strongly. The proposed repressor direction is untested.
E03 places the variant in an active dELS and E05 shows FOXA1 ChIP-seq peaks containing the variant in HepG2. This supports FOXA1 binding to this enhancer-like element.

E17 supports alt T increasing SORT1 in liver, which is consistent with the conditional model that loss of a repressive FOXA1 site derepresses SORT1. However, there is no evidence that FOXA1 represses SORT1 or that FOXA1 loss changes SORT1 expression; the gene link is indirect.

E05 gives FOXA1 expression in the exact DepMap context Hep 3B2.1-7 (53.15 TPM, rank 84/1626) and FOXA1 ChIP peaks in HepG2; E17 shows liver SORT1 eQTLs. This supports the liver/liver-cancer cell context.

The phenotype claim depends on the same unproven assumption that increased SORT1 lowers LDL/MI. E15/E16 are consistent with a lipid association at SORT1, but E18 gives no quoted functional evidence, and the E15 LDL row with effect allele T is directionally discordant.

E10 supports USF1 occupancy at the variant in HepG2 and very high USF1 expression in Hep 3B2.1-7, but there is no allele-specific ChIP or QBiC-SELEX evidence that alt T strengthens USF1 binding. USF1 is one of many bound TFs without a specific allele-model rationale.
E03 places the variant in an active dELS and E10 shows USF1 ChIP-seq peaks containing the variant in HepG2, supporting USF1 occupancy at this enhancer-like element.
E17 supports alt T increasing SORT1 in liver, consistent with an activating USF1-dependent enhancer, but no perturbation or allele-specific evidence shows USF1 mediates the effect on SORT1.
E10 provides USF1 expression in Hep 3B2.1-7 (85.08 TPM, rank 42/1626) and USF1 ChIP peaks in HepG2; E17 shows liver SORT1 eQTLs. This supports the liver/liver-cancer context.

As with the other chains, the lipid/MI phenotype claim rests on the unproven direction that increased SORT1 lowers LDL and MI. E15/E16 are consistent with a SORT1 lipid association, but direct perturbation evidence is absent and E18 has no quoted functional data.

grades_final.reason: E04 shows CEBPA ChIP occupancy at the variant-containing element in HepG2 and E20 shows high CEBPA expression in Hep 3B2.1-7, so occupancy context is present. But there is no QBiC-SELEX or allele-specific ChIP/EMSA showing alt T strengthens CEBPA binding; the alt-direction is motif/literature inference. E19 is only a literature search with titles, not quoted allele-specific C/EBP data. Occupancy without measured allele direction = weak.

E03 directly annotates the variant in EH38E1374646, a dELS with DNase/H3K27ac/H3K4me3 signal, and E04 confirms CEBPA is among the bound factors at this element in HepG2. The element is therefore active and CEBPA-occupied, though E03 z-scores are maxima over biosamples rather than HepG2-specific.

E17 directly shows alt T is associated with higher SORT1 expression in liver (NES +1.27, p 3.1e-54), and E16 gives strong L2G support for SORT1 (0.99). This supports SORT1 as the target gene with the stated alt-T-up direction, though it does not establish CEBPA mediation.

E20 shows CEBPA is highly expressed in the exact DepMap context Hep 3B2.1-7 (141.33 TPM, rank 18/1626), E04 provides HepG2 ChIP occupancy as the stated liver-cancer-line proxy, and E17 shows SORT1 eQTLs in liver.

E15 provides very strong GWAS association at rs12740374 with LDL cholesterol/high cholesterol, and E16 links the locus to lipid traits. However, allele direction is not fully uniform in E15 (most rows list G as effect allele, but one LDL row lists T), and the inference that increased SORT1 lowers LDL is not backed by quoted functional experiments; E18 supplies only titles. This is consistent but indirect and direction-inferential.

E04 supports CEBPA occupancy at the variant element in HepG2 and E20 shows high CEBPA expression in Hep 3B2.1-7. But the claim that alt T strengthens CEBPA binding is not directly measured: no QBiC-SELEX model or allele-specific CEBPA ChIP/EMSA is provided, and E19 only indexes literature by search title. Occupancy without allele-specific direction = weak.

E03 directly places the variant in the active dELS EH38E1374646, and E01 directly annotates the same base as a CELSR2 3_prime_UTR_variant. Together these support the claim that the variant lies in a CELSR2-linked regulatory/transcript region, even though the element-to-CELSR2 regulatory assignment remains plausible rather than proven.

E17 directly shows alt T is associated with higher CELSR2 expression in liver (NES +1.04, p 9.4e-34), and E16 gives high L2G support for CELSR2 (0.96-0.98). This supports CELSR2 as a target gene with the stated direction, though not CEBPA mediation.
E20 establishes high CEBPA expression in Hep 3B2.1-7, E04 provides HepG2 ChIP occupancy in the stated proxy liver-cell context, and E17 shows CELSR2 eQTLs in liver.

E15 and E16 support genetic association of the variant/locus with lipid traits, but there is no quoted functional evidence showing that CELSR2 mediates the LDL/MI phenotype, and the GWAS allele direction in E15 is not fully uniform. E18 provides only literature titles, so the CELSR2-to-phenotype direction remains inferential.

E05 shows FOXA1 ChIP occupancy at the variant-containing element in HepG2 and expression in Hep 3B2.1-7 (53.15 TPM, rank 84/1626). However, the claim that ref G binds FOXA1 more strongly is not measured: no QBiC-SELEX, allele-specific FOXA1 ChIP, or EMSA is provided. This is occupancy plus an unmeasured allele-direction claim = weak.
E03 directly annotates the variant in an active dELS, and E05 directly reports FOXA1 ChIP-seq peaks containing the variant in HepG2. Thus the element is active and FOXA1-occupied.

The only cited gene-level evidence is E17, which shows the variant is associated with SORT1 expression. No cited evidence shows FOXA1 binds and represses SORT1, and the claim itself admits there is no perturbation evidence. The FOXA1-to-SORT1 repression link is therefore unsupported rather than merely indirect.
E05 shows FOXA1 expression in Hep 3B2.1-7 and FOXA1 ChIP occupancy in HepG2, and E17 shows SORT1 eQTLs in liver, supporting the stated liver/hepatocyte-line context.

E15/E16 support variant-level lipid genetic association, but the proposed protective direction through increased SORT1 lowering LDL is inferential and not backed by quoted functional experiments; E15 also contains a non-uniform LDL effect-allele row. E18 provides only titles, so the phenotype link is consistent but weak.

checks.why: This is the most direct way to find quoted allele-specific ChIP, EMSA, reporter, or QBiC-SELEX evidence for the CEBPA direction at rs12740374; such evidence would substantially raise or falsify the CEBPA chain.
E04 establishes CEBPA occupancy only in HepG2, not expression in Hep 3B2.1-7. Exact-context CEBPA expression would determine whether the CEBPA chain's cell-type link is supported or fails.

This would show the Open Targets evidence types linking SORT1 to LDL cholesterol/MI and clarify whether the phenotype step is supported by genetic/functional evidence rather than only L2G and unquoted literature titles.
